tools.name: add_competitor
tools.title: Add competitor
tools.description:
Start tracking a competitor for an extension.

Takes the store and id of a search_catalog row (as external_id), so a
listing you just found can be promoted without looking anything up in
between.

Promoting a listing is what earns it a store fetch: its description,
install count, rating and languages start being recorded, and its
position is kept even on days it falls out of the results entirely.
Where it ranks has been recorded all along, from the searches this
account already runs — so a competitor added today arrives with
history rather than starting from zero.

The description is not available when this returns. Call
list_competitors with the same extension_id until this competitor's
status turns from "pending" to "scraped".

At most 5 competitors per store on the Free
plan and 20 on Premium, because each costs a
fetch of that store on every refresh. The two stores are counted separately.
On plan_limit_reached explain the cap and offer upgrading, or ask which
competitor in that store the user wants removed. Never remove automatically or retry unchanged.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

external_id.description: Chrome's 32-letter id or the AMO slug, as a search_catalog row's id gives it.

tools.name: add_extension
tools.title: Add extension
tools.description:
Track the user's own extension from its Chrome Web Store and/or Firefox Add-ons URL.
Resolve a name with search_catalog first; pass the selected result's url. Do not guess
between ambiguous listings or start tracking research results without the user's request.

Supply both URLs in one call only when they are the same product: they share one
extension_id and consume one plan slot. Repeating an existing URL is a no-op, including
at the cap. If one URL matches existing tracking, its missing store is attached and
existing keywords are adopted. Conflicting listings are refused, never replaced or merged.

Free allows 1 tracked extension; Premium allows 10.
The response includes current usage and limits. A plan_limit_reached error is not retryable
unchanged: explain it, offer the pricing link, or ask which existing extension the user
wants removed with remove_extension. Never delete tracking automatically to free a slot.

Cached metrics may be available immediately; fresh metrics run in the background.
Use get_extension and list_scrape_runs to check progress; do not promise a completion time.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

chrome_url.description: HTTPS Chrome Web Store listing URL; at least one store URL is required.

firefox_url.description: HTTPS Firefox Add-ons listing URL, optionally paired with the same product's Chrome URL.

tools.name: add_keyword
tools.title: Add keyword
tools.description:
Start tracking a search term for an extension. The term is added once
per store the extension is listed in, and a rank fetch is enqueued for
each store that was not already tracking it.

The position is not available when this returns. Call list_keywords with
the same extension_id until this term's status turns from "pending" to
"scanned", or list_scrape_runs to watch the fetch itself — a fetch that
fails shows up there, rather than as a position that never arrives.

A term is tracked per store language. Tracking "ad blocker" in en and
again in de gives two independent keywords with their own positions.
Call list_keywords for the languages an extension already tracks.

An extension tracks at most 10 keywords on the
Free plan and 50 on Premium, counted per
language: "ad blocker" in en and de is two. Past that this returns a limit
error. Explain the limit and offer upgrading, or ask which keyword the
user wants removed with remove_keyword. Never remove automatically or retry unchanged.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

term.description: The search term, e.g. "json viewer". Squished and lowercased before use.

locale.description: Store language to search in: "en", "de", "pt-BR". Defaults to "en". The same term ranks differently in each, so this is a separate keyword, not a translation. Canonicalised before use, so "DE" and "de" are one keyword and "pt-br" comes back as "pt-BR".

tools.name: get_extension
tools.title: Get extension
tools.description:
One extension in full: every store listing's latest numbers plus its
tracked keywords and their current positions.

Each listing's rank is its position by users within its store, computed
from the current user count; ties share a rank (rank_tied = others at the
same count); rank_change is the move since last week's recorded rank.

locales lists every store language this extension tracks, with a
keyword count each, so the keywords can be worked a language at a time.

Use get_metrics_history or get_keyword_ranks for movement over time.

This is the tracked view, built from what we have recorded. For an
extension this account does not track, use get_listing instead.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

tools.name: get_keyword_ranks
tools.title: Get keyword ranks
tools.description:
Daily search position history for an extension's tracked keywords, one
series per term per store.

Every point carries the depth it was scanned to, because a position only
means something against the size of the pool it came from: #1 of 9 and
#1 of 50 are different results. A null position means we searched that
deep and this extension was not in the results.

A term tracked in more than one store language comes back as one series
per language — the same term is a different SERP in each.

Each series has a source. "store" is the store's own search. "google" is
where the listing page ranks in Google: organic results only (ads and
other blocks are not counted), top 50, desktop, in the keyword
language's country (English: the United States). A null Google position
means Google was searched 50 deep and the listing was not there.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

term.description: One term. Omit for all of them.

locale.description: Store language, e.g. "de". Omit for every language. Canonicalised before use, so "DE" and "de" are one keyword and "pt-br" comes back as "pt-BR".

source.description: Store search or Google. Omit for both.

days.description: How far back to look. Defaults to 30.

tools.name: get_keyword_serp
tools.title: Get keyword serp
tools.description:
The search page for one of an extension's tracked keywords, as this
account last recorded it — who was on it, in what order, and which way
each of them moved over the past week.

Read from recorded history, not from the store: no fetch, no waiting,
no egress spent. Use this when you want movement, or the same page the
dashboard is showing.

Every row carries mine and competitor flags, so "who is above me and
which of them am I already tracking" is one call. Positions always
travel with depth_scanned, because #1 of 9 and #1 of 50 are different
results.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

term.description: A term this extension tracks. From list_keywords.

window.description: Return only the leaders and our own neighbourhood rather than the whole page. Defaults to false.

tools.name: get_listing
tools.title: Get listing
tools.description:
One extension's full listing from the catalog -- any extension, tracked by this account or
not: description, users, rating, reviews, version, languages, categories, permissions and
publisher. Pass the store and id of a search_catalog row as store and external_id.
rank is the position by users within the store; ties share a rank (rank_tied = others at the same
count); recomputed weekly on rank_on; rank_change is the move since the week before, positive = up.

English copy, refreshed weekly from the store; refreshed_at says when. This never fetches,
never answers "pending" and never starts tracking. users, rating and reviews are null when
the store shows no number, which is not zero. For an extension this account tracks,
get_metrics_history has its numbers over time. Shares search_catalog's
60 calls a minute per account.

Works without an account too.

external_id.description: Chrome's 32-letter id or the AMO slug, as a search_catalog row's id gives it.

tools.name: get_metrics_history
tools.title: Get metrics history
tools.description:
Daily-or-sparser history of an extension's numbers: user count,
rating and ratings count, each as a map of ISO date to value.
"listings" is this extension's own store listings; "competitors" is
its roster from list_competitors. store and days filter both.

A map holds only dates actually observed; an empty map means no
measurement in range, never zero. If users_rounded_in_range is true
the store published rounded counts somewhere in the window, so small
movements there may be rounding.

Competitors are captured every few days rather than daily, and not on
a fixed schedule, so compare a rival against "listings" on dates
present in both, never by position in the map. Join a competitor
entry back to list_competitors on (store, external_id); name is a
label, not an identifier.

include_competitors adds every roster competitor's history.
competitors narrows that to specific (store, external_id) pairs and
implies include_competitors; a pair not on the roster fails the whole
call rather than silently dropping it.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

store.description: Filters both listings and competitors. Omit for every store.

days.description: How far back to look. Defaults to 30.

include_competitors.description: Also return history for this extension's promoted competitors. Defaults to false.

competitors.description: Limit competitor history to these (store, external_id) pairs from list_competitors. Implies include_competitors; an unlisted pair fails the call.

tools.name: list_competitors
tools.title: List competitors
tools.description:
Who this extension competes with, measured across every keyword it
tracks.

Two sets. "competitors" is the roster you promoted with
add_competitor: their descriptions, install counts and ratings are
recorded, and their positions are kept even on days they fall out of
the results. "candidates" — returned only with include_observed —
is everyone else who has appeared in those searches, ranked by how
often they beat you.

Both are read from positions this account already recorded, not from
the store: no fetch, no waiting, and each row carries the evidence
behind it (how many of your terms, average position, first seen). This
is the tool for deciding who is worth promoting.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

include_observed.description: Also return unpromoted candidates. Defaults to false.

tools.name: list_extensions
tools.title: List extensions
tools.description:
Every extension this token's owner tracks, with each store listing's
latest numbers: user count (and whether the store rounded it), the
7-day change, rating, ratings count and category rank.

Start here when this connection has an account: every tracking tool
takes an extension_id from this list.
Includes effective plan limits and extension usage (null caps mean unlimited).
If empty, help the user choose a store listing and call add_extension when asked.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

tools.name: list_keywords
tools.title: List keywords
tools.description:
Every search term tracked for one extension, one row per term per store.

status is "pending" until a fetch has landed since the term was tracked,
and "scanned" once one has. A "scanned" row with a null position means
we searched depth_scanned results and this extension was not among
them — that is a real observation, not missing data.

A "pending" row can still carry a position. Removing a keyword stops the
tracking but keeps the history, so a term tracked before and added again
arrives with its previous result already in place; captured_on says how
old that is. Poll until the status reads "scanned" to know the number
answers the current tracking.

locale is the store language the term was searched in. The same term
ranks differently under hl=de than under hl=en, so two rows sharing a
term and a store are two different results.

locales lists every store language this extension tracks, with a
keyword count each — start there to work a language at a time. It
always reports every language, including when the locale argument
narrows the rows to one.

search_volume is Google Ads' average monthly searches for the term in
the row's store language: for English, in the United States or
worldwide as the account's profile setting says (United States unless
changed), and in one country for the others (Germany for de, Spain for
es, Brazil for pt-BR, and so on).
It is web search demand, not searches inside the store, and is the same
for both stores. null means not fetched yet, Google has no data, or the
term can't be looked up (symbols such as + or %, over 80 characters or
10 words, or a store language Google Ads has no country for, such as
ru); search_volume_fetched_at says which.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

locale.description: Store language, e.g. "de". Omit for every language. Canonicalised before use, so "DE" and "de" are one keyword and "pt-br" comes back as "pt-BR".

tools.name: list_scrape_runs
tools.title: List scrape runs
tools.description:
Recent scrape attempts against your own extensions, newest first, with
their outcome and any error. Covers both the listing fetches and the
rank fetches for the search terms they track.

Use this after add_keyword to watch the rank fetch: the run is targeted
at the search term, and a failed fetch appears here as a failure rather
than as a position that never arrives.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

extension_id.description: Narrow to one extension's listings and tracked keywords.

tools.name: remove_competitor
tools.title: Remove competitor
tools.description:
Stop tracking a competitor for an extension.

Stops the store fetches. The recorded history is kept, so adding the
same competitor again later restores its charts rather than starting
from zero — and its positions carry on being observed either way,
because they come from searches this account already runs.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

tools.name: remove_extension
tools.title: Remove extension
tools.description:
Stop tracking one of this account's extensions, using an extension_id from list_extensions.
Remove only the extension the user asked to remove; clarify ambiguous names first.
Never remove an extension automatically to make room at a plan limit.

This deletes this account's extension record, notes, keyword tracking and competitor
configuration for it, across both stores. Re-adding does not restore that configuration.
Shared store listings, collected metrics/rank history and other users' tracking remain.
A missing or already removed id returns the same error as another account's id.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

extension_id.description: The user's chosen extension_id from list_extensions.

tools.name: remove_keyword
tools.title: Remove keyword
tools.description:
Stop tracking a search term for an extension, across every store it was
tracked in. Positions already recorded are kept; only the tracking stops.

Other extensions tracking the same term are unaffected, including ones
that track the same store listing: every extension's keywords are its own.

A term is tracked per store language. Tracking "ad blocker" in en and
again in de gives two independent keywords with their own positions.
Call list_keywords for the languages an extension already tracks.

Needs an ExtensionDash account: sign in from your app, e.g. `claude mcp login extensions-dashboard` or `codex mcp login extensions-dashboard`.

locale.description: Store language to search in: "en", "de", "pt-BR". Defaults to "en". The same term ranks differently in each, so this is a separate keyword, not a translation. Canonicalised before use, so "DE" and "de" are one keyword and "pt-br" comes back as "pt-BR".

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.title: Search catalog
tools.description:
Search one store's catalog of extensions fetched so far, for market and niche research:
store "chrome" (default) or "firefox", one per call -- Chrome users are a rounded weekly
count, Firefox's an exact daily average, so the two are never mixed. listed and known in
each answer show how much of that store the catalog covers.
rank is the position by users within the store; ties share a rank (rank_tied = others at the same
count); recomputed weekly on rank_on; rank_change is the move since the week before, positive = up.

Filter by name words (match "all" or "any"; case and punctuation are ignored, and an exact
name comes first unless you sort), by one category of that store (a slug such as
"productivity/developer" or "privacy-security"; an unknown one is refused with the store's
list) and by inclusive ranges on users, rating, reviews, language count and description
length; sort by any of those or by last update. This never fetches the store. users,
rating and reviews are null when the store shows no number, which is not zero. Each row
says whether it is one of yours or a competitor you track; pass its store and id to
add_competitor to start tracking it. For one extension's full listing, call get_listing.

Allows 60 calls a minute per account.

Works without an account too.

category.description: One category slug of the chosen store, as rows return it.

sort.description: Defaults to users, with an exact name match first when query is given.

dir.description: Defaults to desc. Nulls always last.
